chase: Stay near the wall and I won't have to go around you.
I won't come closer while you're watching. I'll go around instead.
You're in my way now. I'm sorry, but I have to stop you.
I'm closing the gap slowly. I have no reason to hurry.
If I'm cornered, I stop and wait. I don't push through you.
I keep my distance when you're in sight. It's only polite.
I'm not trying to catch you. I just can't let you pass.
Slowly now. I'm coming around the shelf, but not too fast.
You can run if you like. I'll just keep walking after you.
I'm sorry about the corner. I don't mean to trap you there.
Behind the shelf is a dead end. You don't want to go there.
Don't mind me. I'm only following the path to the next room.
I'll stay three steps back. That's close enough to watch you.
The battery isn't moving. Neither am I. We'll see who gets there.
I'm not running at you. I'm only going to the battery behind you.
I won't come closer while you're in the light.
Keep to the wall, please. I'll wait at the turn.
The landing is long. You won't reach the top.
catch: Oh, I've got you. Stay still and I'll be gentle about it.
I didn't want it to be you. I'm sorry.
Hold still now. I'll walk you back to the entrance.
You're out now. Please be careful on the stairs going down.
Got you. Hold still, the others will want to know.
That's one more we won't see on this floor again.
You stopped moving, so it was easy. I'm sorry.
Let go of the crate. You can't hold on to this place.
Your run is over here. I'll walk you out, quietly.
Another one just went out. I'm sorry for them.
Your friend just got pulled out. Try not to panic.
It's quiet once someone is taken. I don't enjoy that part.
I caught you, and I'm sorry it had to be me.
Someone is out now. I'll keep the room for them.
You were fast, but not quite fast enough this time.
Hush, now. I'm so sorry about this.
Got you by the wrist. You're safe enough here.
I caught you. Let's sit until it passes.
hear: I heard a door on the landing. I'm going to look.
That was a shout. I'll go and see who it was.
Something broke in the next room. I'll check it now.
Footsteps on the stairs. Light ones, a runner's steps.
A drawer slid open somewhere. I'll go look inside.
That sound came from the room with the lamp. Going now.
Something knocked twice behind the cabinet. I'm listening.
Quiet, but not quiet enough. I heard you on the carpet.
Glass broke down the hall. I'm walking over to it.
A door closed upstairs. I'll see what's behind it.
I heard a whisper near the vent. Let me look.
That noise was too loud for an empty floor. Going.
Someone's running in the hall. I'll go listen closer.
The shelf rattled. I'll come and see what moved.
Something creaked on the stairs. I'll check.
A cup clinked in the parlor. Who's there?
Shout from the balcony. I'm going over.
search: You lost me around the corner. I'll wait here until you come out.
I can't see you now. I'll check the room again.
Where did you go? I'll look under the beds first.
I'm sniffing around the shelves. Someone was here recently.
The trail stops at the door. I'll search this corner.
Nothing in the cupboard. I'll try the next room.
I'll go back to my rounds now. Maybe you'll come out.
I've lost you for now. I'll keep looking, slowly.
Empty room. I'll go back and check the landing.
You're somewhere close. I can feel it in the air.
I'll look behind every crate until I find you.
Quiet again. I'll finish my rounds and listen for you.
I'll return to the battery route and listen as I go.
I'm patient. I'll wait here and see who moves.
Lost you. That's all right, I know this floor well.
stunned: Ow. That was a crowbar, I think. Give me a second.
My legs aren't working right. Wait, let me steady myself.
The buzz is still in my arms. I'll shake it off.
Give me one moment. My head feels full of static.
That hit my joints. I need a moment to reset.
I can't move well after that. Please give me a moment.
Stunned, but not gone. I'll be back on my feet soon.
Oh, my sensors are rattling. Hold on, I'm recovering.
That's a bad jolt. I'll stand here until it passes.
My arm is locked up. Let me try moving it again.
The axe clanged off my shell. Give me a second.
Hold still. I'll be fine, just a little dizzy.
I'm shaking it off. You didn't hit me that hard.
Taser again. I'll remember that the next time we meet.
I can stand. My balance is just slipping a little.
hide_spot: Oh, you're hiding. Stand very still behind the crate, then.
Hiding is nice. It's quiet in there. I don't mind the wait.
You've been hiding a while. I'll look somewhere else for now.
I can see your shoes under the bed. Sorry about that.
The locker is shaking a little. I'll leave it closed.
I know hiding spots. I used to rest in cupboards too.
Behind the bed is the first place I'd check.
I'll walk past this locker. Breathe quietly, please.
Please don't hold your breath in there. You'll get dizzy.
I see the bed sheet moving. I'll pretend I didn't.
The wardrobe door is open just a crack. Close it.
Every hiding place has someone waiting. This one has you.
I'll stand by the door and listen for a while.
You tucked yourself in nicely. I'll give you that.
I'm going to keep walking. You can come out soon.
light: Your light is on. I can see it from the stairs.
Please turn the flashlight off. You're lighting up the whole room.
You shone that light straight at me. I'll look away now.
Your flashlight makes a shadow on the wall. You're closer than you think.
The light is in my eyes. I can't see the shelf now.
Oh, that's bright. Please point it somewhere else.
I'm dazzled for a moment. Give me a second to adjust.
That beam hurts a little. Could you lower it, please?
Turn the light down. I'm trying to watch the stairs.
Your beam is hitting my face. I'll turn my head.
Too much light in this corridor. I'm squinting, that's all.
I can't see anything past that flashlight. Stop it, please.
Every time that light flicks on, I lose my footing.
You're blinding me. I'll step back until my eyes adjust.
Lamp light is nice on a shelf. Not on me, though.
idle: The stairs are my favorite place to sit with my box.
I know where every pen in this home came from.
People reach for the things they had. I understand that.
I like to play a moment back in my head, slowly, like a reel.
Some people forget small things quickly. I hold on to mine.
A small thing with a memory attached is worth more than a full box.
Ask me where something came from, and I'll tell you if I know.
Each of you has a favorite spot. I know all of them.
Between us, the others leave the lights on far too long.
Someone left a glove on the stairs. I saved it for them.
My box holds small things. Each one is somebody's story.
I keep the things testers leave behind, so somebody remembers them.
The others move too fast. They step right past things worth keeping.
Some of them think batteries are just batteries. They aren't.
Don't tell the others I stopped to look at the picture frame.
ability: There's a battery under the far shelf. I'm closer than you are.
Sorry, that one's mine. I was walking toward it first.
I'm heading for the nearest battery. Please don't get in my way.
Two more batteries on this floor. I can reach both before you.
Oh, that battery is still warm. Someone was just holding it.
I'll only take what's uncollected. Leave the rest alone, please.
Every battery on this floor has a place. I'm going to its place.
You reached the cabinet. I was already halfway to the drawer.
A battery left on a table is a battery waiting for me.
The nearest one is in the corner. I can see it from here.
Batteries don't walk, but I'm very good at getting to them.
Six steps to the battery. Four if you move out of the doorway.
Once I take a battery, it stays gone from the floor for good.
Get too close to a battery and I'll have it before you blink.
The battery's on the carpet now. Almost in reach. Almost mine.
mechanic: The lamp is on, so that battery is easy to spot for us both.
Careful at the cabinet. There's a battery behind that drawer, mine.
I can hear one battery humming on the landing. That's mine.
A relay with no battery is just a box. I'll take the battery.
Relays go dark when their batteries leave the floor.
Radar pings are louder near the stairs. Watch the signal.
Vents are cold tonight. Nobody should trust the ducts.
That door sticks on the third try. I know the trick.
Stairs are slippery near the landing. Take them slowly.
Drop that battery and I'll be the one to pick it up.
That tool on the shelf fits the charger by the vent.
Once a door is opened, it stays open for everyone.
The radar blinks when I walk past the broken panel.
Pulling the fuse box would dim every lamp on the floor.
Leave the charger alone. It's the only one still warm.
The cabinet drawer has a battery. Careful with it.
The relay sits under the lamp. Turn it on first.
Relay panel is behind the cabinet. Be careful.
